introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Further Mathematics Paper 2 (0775), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2026. Duration: three hours.**

Answer ALL 10 questions. For your guidance, the approximate mark allocation for parts of each question is indicated. Mathematical formulae and tables published by the Board, and noiseless non-programmable electronic calculators are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The vectors $\mathbf a = \mathbf i - 4\mathbf j + 2\mathbf k$, $\mathbf b = p\mathbf i - 3\mathbf j + q\mathbf k$ and $\mathbf c = p\mathbf i + \mathbf j - q\mathbf k$, where $p, q \in \mathbb R$, are such that $\mathbf a$ is perpendicular to both $\mathbf b$ and $\mathbf c$.

Find the values of the scalars $p$ and $q$. *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Two vectors are perpendicular exactly when their scalar product is zero.

$$\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b = (1)(p) + (-4)(-3) + (2)(q) = p + 12 + 2q = 0 \qquad (1)$$

$$\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf c = (1)(p) + (-4)(1) + (2)(-q) = p - 4 - 2q = 0 \qquad (2)$$

Add (1) and (2): $2p + 8 = 0$, so $p = -4$.

Substitute into (1): $-4 + 12 + 2q = 0$, so $2q = -8$ and $q = -4$.

**Check in (2):** $-4 - 4 - 2(-4) = -8 + 8 = 0$. ✓

$$\boxed{p = -4,\quad q = -4}$$

so $\mathbf b = -4\mathbf i - 3\mathbf j - 4\mathbf k$ and $\mathbf c = -4\mathbf i + \mathbf j + 4\mathbf k$.

questions.enonce_markdown: With these values of $p$ and $q$, find the Cartesian equation of the plane containing the position vectors $\mathbf a$, $\mathbf b$ and $\mathbf c$. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The plane contains the three points $A$, $B$, $C$ whose position vectors are $\mathbf a = (1, -4, 2)$, $\mathbf b = (-4, -3, -4)$, $\mathbf c = (-4, 1, 4)$ (they are the endpoints of the vectors, so the plane does not necessarily pass through the origin).

**Two vectors in the plane.**

$$\overrightarrow{AB} = \mathbf b - \mathbf a = (-5, 1, -6), \qquad \overrightarrow{AC} = \mathbf c - \mathbf a = (-5, 5, 2).$$

**Normal vector.**

$$\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{AC} = \begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i & \mathbf j & \mathbf k\\ -5 & 1 & -6\\ -5 & 5 & 2\end{vmatrix} = \mathbf i(2 + 30) - \mathbf j(-10 - 30) + \mathbf k(-25 + 5) = (32, 40, -20).$$

Divide by $4$: a normal is $\mathbf n = (8, 10, -5)$.

**Equation.** $\mathbf r\cdot\mathbf n = \mathbf a\cdot\mathbf n$, with $\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf n = 8(1) + 10(-4) - 5(2) = -42$. So

$$\boxed{8x + 10y - 5z = -42}$$

**Check** with $B$: $8(-4) + 10(-3) - 5(-4) = -32 - 30 + 20 = -42$ ✓; with $C$: $8(-4) + 10(1) - 5(4) = -32 + 10 - 20 = -42$ ✓.
